title: John Boger’s “Self-Infect My Mind” spins overthinking into an addictive dancefloor confession
htmlContent:
John Boger's latest single, "Self-Infect My Mind," is a track that catches you off guard. It sounds like a lively dance-pop song at first, with an upbeat rhythm that naturally makes you want to move. But if you listen more closely, you'll notice it carries a deeper, personal message about the tiring habit of worrying too much about what others think of you. While it makes you want to dance, the song also takes you on an inner journey, exploring the struggles of overthinking. The lyrics dig into the anxious thoughts that often keep us up at night.

The tension between feeling unsure of ourselves and wanting to express who we are makes the music even more powerful. There's a raw honesty in the lyrics that many people can relate to. Now, let's talk about the singing. It's not perfect or overly polished, and that's okay. In fact, those little imperfections add to the song's appeal. They make it feel more genuine and urgent, like the whirlwind of thoughts we often have late at night. The slightly offbeat vocals reflect the chaos of overthinking, making "Self-Infect My Mind" feel even more real.

https://open.spotify.com/track/12i36tn1SBWhwedanNiZDd

The music has a strong dance vibe, keeping the energy high and making it hard to stay still. The beat flows like a racing mind while the melodies come in and out, mimicking how our thoughts can endlessly loop when we can't shake off an idea. It beautifully balances deep reflection with the joy of letting loose. "Self-Infect My Mind" is about feeling stuck in your own head, but ironically, it also offers a sense of freedom. It encourages you to embrace your messy thoughts and, for just a little while, to set them aside and dance.
